html:
A caravan town on the Adrar plateau of Mauritania, founded in its present form in the 13th century, known for its old stone mosque and family libraries of Arabic manuscripts.

It was a meeting place for pilgrims leaving for Mecca and a stop on the trans-Saharan trade routes. Its scholars were so well known that the Arab world called the whole land of the Moors bilad Shinqit, the land of Chinguetti. With the old towns of Ouadane, Tichitt and Walata it became a World Heritage Site in 1996. Sand dunes now press on its streets, and families still guard manuscripts on law, astronomy and poetry, like the Timbuktu manuscripts. See also Islam.
sum: A caravan town on the Adrar plateau of Mauritania, founded in its present form in the 13th century, known for its old stone mosque and family libraries of Arabic manuscripts.
